QC cases log

Jaime Abraham Castro-Mondragon & Jean-Marc Costanzi

Last update: 2026-06-01


1 Introduction


This document shows a list of special cases that are recurrently observed during the process of DNA variants QC.

The document is divided in different categories:

  • Possible contamination
  • …

Each example contains a paragraph with the biological or technical explanation of the case and its solution (i.e., how to proceed in case we encounter one case of these during the QC process).

This document will be regularly expanded as more special cases are detected during the DNA variants QC process.


2 Concepts

  • VAF: Variant Allele Frequency. The proportion of sequencing reads that display a specific genetic variant compared to the total reads at that specific genomic location,


3 Possible Contamination


TSOPPI estimates the level of contamination in each samples, a contamination score and its corresponding p-value are calculated. When a sample is above the predefined thresholds, it is tagged as contamination (Figure 1).

Figure 1. Example of samples tagged as contaminated (TSOPPI output)



3.1 Real Low Contamination


This is an example of real yet low degree contamination. The plot in Figure 2 shows the VAF of variants within a sample (y-axis) along the genome (x-axis, chromosomes).

The area highlighted in the red box shows that many variants in this samples have a VAF near of 0.1. In normal conditions, we expect to observe a few variants with this value, however when many variants have similar VAF along the whole genome we can suspect a case of true contamination.


Explanation: it is likely that these variants with low VAF correspond to another sample, this is a clear signal of contamination.


Solution: as in this case the contamination degree is low, we suggest to discard all the mutations in this sample with low VAF (< 0.2).

Figure 2. Example of samples tagged as contaminated (TSOPPI output)
